ca_box_canyon_east.blurb: Box Canyon East is the busiest part of New Jack City, a sport climbing destination in the high desert near Barstow at roughly 3,600 feet. Nearly everything is bolted single-pitch sport, with a few boulder problems, trad and top-rope lines on the side. Grades run from about 5.6 to 5.13, with the heart of the area in the 5.10 to 5.12 range and a modest supply of moderates. Dozens of small crags are spread around, among them Raven Rocks, Boy Scout Wall, Fairway and Crossfire Crag. Approaches are short, from a minute to about twenty, and the crowds thin the farther you walk. Cooler months are best, since summer heat is intense and walls warm quickly by midday.

co_four_corners_area.blurb: The Four Corners Area covers southwest Colorado around Cortez, Mesa Verde and the Dolores River canyon. Bouldering accounts for about half the climbs and trad for over a third, with only a little sport. Boulder problems mostly sit between V0 and V4, and the roped climbs cluster around 5.10 and 5.11 with some easier options. The Dolores River Canyon has quality Wingate sandstone with a traditional, ground-up style, mostly one or two pitches with short approaches; its east and northeast faces can feel chilly in winter. Around Cortez, bouldering on potholed sandstone is scattered and best for a quick session rather than a destination trip. Expect a spread-out region with a quiet, remote feel.

ky_western_kentucky.blurb: Western Kentucky climbing is varied and spread out across many small areas, reached off the interstate and parkway network. Sport routes make up the largest share, followed by bouldering and trad, with a few top-rope and aid lines. Sport climbs concentrate in the 5.9 to 5.12 range, centered on 5.10, while boulder problems are mostly V2 to V4. Hunter Bluff and The Oasis carry substantial sport climbing. Clifty Hollow, near Bowling Green, is best known for boulders and variations, with a set of newer bouldery, pumpy sport routes of 30 to 40 feet. Shanty Hollow is a small, low-key bouldering spot by a lake where the stone is friable and mossy, with plenty of cleaning still to do.

mt_west_side.blurb: West Side covers the west bank of Gallatin Canyon in southwest Montana, where the rock is quality gneiss. Most of the climbing is bouldering, with problems from V0 into the V10 range and the weight at V3 to V5. Cascade Creek is the largest sub-area, an alpine boulder field in a talus slope reached by the Lava Lake trail, and the Nunnery adds another bouldering zone along the river. The roped climbing is smaller than on the east side and mostly trad, from 5.8 to 5.13, with Gallatin Tower offering multi-pitch lines and the Cube holding sport routes. The Dregs adds a few more trad lines. Expect a mix of short roadside outings and longer walks into the boulders.

ny_d_keene_valley_and_chapel_pond.blurb: Keene Valley and Chapel Pond is the Adirondacks' main ice climbing zone, with the largest concentration of ice routes in the park. The cliffs line the Route 73 corridor from the Northway toward Lake Placid. Ice dominates, with a smaller group of mixed routes. Grades center on WI3 and WI4, with a modest number at WI2, WI5 and a few harder, and the mixed climbs run from M3 to M7. Routes range from single pitches to multi-pitch outings. Chapel Pond has the most lines, and Chapel Pond Canyon, reached across the frozen pond, holds harder routes. Cascade Pass and the north face of Pitchoff add further options. Ice here forms early and is dependable through winter.

on_mount_nemo.blurb: Mount Nemo is a cliff on the Niagara Escarpment southwest of Toronto and one of the most historic and visited climbing areas in Canada. Sport routes are the majority, with a large trad share and a couple of top-ropes. Most climbs fall between 5.9 and 5.12, with a heavy concentration at 5.10 and 5.11 and a decent set of easier lines. Climbing here is sustained and varied, with edges, cracks, steep walls with reachy jugs and slabby arêtes. The cliff is one long line broken by gullies, split into sub-areas such as The Turtle, Dance Wall, The Big Gulp and Iguana Wall. Spring is especially popular because the walls catch afternoon and evening sun.
